Biogas, produced from landfills, wastewater, manure, and other organic wastes, is used to generate electricity for on-site use or sold to the grid. In 2024, solid wood and wood waste and black liquor accounted for 68% of total biomass power generation, landfill gas was 16%, and the organic portion of municipal solid waste was 12% (EIA 2025i). DOE’s Alternative Fuels and Feedstocks Office funds the Billion-Ton Report—a comprehensive feedstock analysis report of potential biomass feedstock resources in the United States inclusive of price, quantity, geographic location and distribution, and market maturity. Other biomass includes other biomass solids, other biomass gases, agricultural crop residues, sludge waste, wood-waste liquids, and other biomass liquids. 2.3 Economic Impacts and Jobs The economic impacts for ethanol, biodiesel, renewable diesel, SAF, and RNG are available from their respective industry organizations. These studies use IMPLAN—an economic input- output model—to estimate gross value added (total value of the goods and services produced by businesses), income, and employment resulting from the various types of alternative fuels produced annually. The following summarizes information provided by the Renewable Fuels Association (RFA), Clean Fuels Association of America, and Renewable Natural Gas Coalition: • The ethanol industry’s 2024 contribution to the economy was $53 billion to gross domestic product, $28.3 billion in household income, and $10.3 billion in taxes (RFA 2025c). In 2024 it supported 55,810 direct jobs and 258,089 indirect/induced jobs, two- thirds of which were agriculture based. • The 2024 economic impact for biodiesel, renewable diesel, and SAF production was $42 billion in economic activity, supporting 107,400 jobs and $5.8 billion in wages paid (GlobalData 2025). • RNG’s contribution includes an estimated 55,000 jobs and $7 billion to gross domestic product.
